title: Partition to K Equal Sum Subsets
prompt: Given an integer array `nums` and an integer `k`, return true if it is possible to divide this array into `k` non-empty subsets whose sums are all equal.

examples.explanation: It's possible to divide it into 4 subsets each with sum 5: (1,4), (5), (2,3), (2,3).
The total is 10, which isn't divisible by 3, so equal-sum subsets are impossible.

constraints: The frequency of each element is in the range [1, 4]
hints: First check the total sum is divisible by k; if not, return false immediately without searching.
Sort nums in descending order and try filling k buckets (each targeting total/k) one number at a time — placing larger numbers first prunes far more aggressively than placing small ones.

Skip failed duplicate states: if placing a number into an empty bucket fails, don't bother trying it in any other currently-empty bucket (they're equivalent), and skip re-trying an already-used number at the same recursion level.

solution.approach: Compute the target subset sum as total/k (returning false immediately if it doesn't divide evenly, or if any single number exceeds it). Sort nums descending so large, highly-constraining values are placed first, causing dead-end branches to be pruned near the top of the search tree rather than deep inside it. Backtrack by choosing, for each not-yet-used number in order, which of k bucket sums to add it to; skip a bucket if adding would exceed the target, and skip trying an empty bucket more than once at a given step (all empty buckets are interchangeable, so a failure in one implies failure in any other empty one). Success is reached when every number has been placed and all k buckets equal the target exactly.
solution.timeComplexity: O(k^n) worst case, heavily pruned in practice
solution.spaceComplexity: O(n) recursion depth, O(k) for bucket sums
